import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the dataset
data = pd.read_csv('data/customer_segments.csv')

# Create a new column for total spending
data['Total_Spending'] = (data['MntWines'] + data['MntFruits'] + data['MntMeatProducts'] +

# Plot: Distribution of Total Spending by Education Level

# Customize the plot
plt.title('Distribution of Total Spending by Education Level', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Education', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Total Spending', fontsize=12)
plt.xticks(rotation=45)
plt.grid(axis='y', linestyle='--', alpha=0.7)

import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the dataset
data = pd.read_csv('data/customer_segments.csv')

# Create a new column for total spending
data['Total_Spending'] = (data['MntWines'] + data['MntFruits'] + data['MntMeatProducts'] + 
                          data['MntFishProducts'] + data['MntSweetProducts'] + data['MntGoldProds'])

# Plot: Distribution of Total Spending by Education Level
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
sns.boxplot(data=data, x='Education', y='Total_Spending', palette='muted')

# Customize the plot
plt.title('Distribution of Total Spending by Education Level', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Education', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Total Spending', fontsize=12)
plt.xticks(rotation=45)
plt.grid(axis='y', linestyle='--', alpha=0.7)

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
